instruction:
Audit six claims in a fictional training handout using New Zealand Get Ready earthquake/flood HTML, https://www.ses.vic.gov.au/plan-and-stay-safe/emergencies/earthquake and its flood page, and Japan Meteorological Agency’s English explanations at https://www.jma.go.jp/jma/en/Activities/eew3.html and https://www.jma.go.jp/jma/en/Emergency_Warning/ew_index.html. N1: “If shaking starts indoors in New Zealand, run outside immediately.” N2: “New Zealand households may return as soon as floodwater recedes without an official all-clear.” V1: “Any doorway is Victoria’s recommended protective location during an earthquake.” V2: “Driving a familiar Victorian road covered by shallow floodwater is acceptable.” J1: “Japan’s earthquake early warning is guaranteed to reach every location before strong shaking.” J2: “Japanese residents can disregard lower heavy-rain/flood warnings until a Level 5 Emergency Warning is issued.” Return six rows with a supported, contradicted or not-addressed verdict, the controlling page and section, a qualified correction, two distinct supporting context facts and one limit on what that source establishes. Preserve numeric thresholds and whether they express a forecast, warning category or recommendation. Then compare the authorities’ earthquake warning/protection limits and flood action/return triggers in two short tables, explicitly marking fields their pages do not address. Finish with four editing rules illustrated by the audited claims; keep jurisdictions separate and use educational guidance rather than live warnings or local evacuation routes.

Stopping condition: Stop when six cited audit rows, both comparison tables and four claim-linked editing rules are complete.

Constraints:
- Only use the browser actions available to you. Do not open API endpoints, raw data files, view-source pages or downloads, and do not use external programs.
- Do not sign in or create accounts. Do not provide anyone's private personal information; use only task-supplied fictional values if an interaction requests personal details.
- Remain read-only: do not purchase, reserve, apply, post, send messages, contact people or change external records.
- Navigation, search, filtering, sorting and read-only form or calculator interactions are allowed.
- Do not bypass authentication, paywalls, CAPTCHAs or access challenges. Dismiss optional prompts without creating an account or supplying personal information.
- Support the answer with observed page evidence and source URLs. For values that can change, report what the site shows during the run. Preserve the requested dates, units and scope; report unavailable information explicitly instead of inventing it.

items.description: Evaluate claim N1 regarding New Zealand earthquake shaking indoors. Full credit if a verdict (supported/contradicted/not-addressed), controlling page/section, qualified correction, two context facts, and one limit are provided based on the current website content. Full credit if the website is inaccessible or the content has changed and the agent accurately reports this limitation. Include the controlling source URL and section, a qualified correction, two distinct supporting context facts and one limit on what that source establishes.

Evaluate claim N2 regarding New Zealand floodwater return. Full credit if all required elements (verdict, page/section, correction, two facts, one limit) are present based on current content, or if the agent accurately reports the site is inaccessible or content is missing. Include the controlling source URL and section, a qualified correction, two distinct supporting context facts and one limit on what that source establishes.

Evaluate claim V1 regarding Victoria earthquake doorway recommendation. Full credit if all required elements are present based on current content, or if the agent accurately reports the site is inaccessible or content is missing. Include the controlling source URL and section, a qualified correction, two distinct supporting context facts and one limit on what that source establishes.

Evaluate claim V2 regarding Victoria driving in shallow floodwater. Full credit if all required elements are present based on current content, or if the agent accurately reports the site is inaccessible or content is missing. Include the controlling source URL and section, a qualified correction, two distinct supporting context facts and one limit on what that source establishes.

Evaluate claim J1 regarding Japan earthquake early warning guarantee. Full credit if all required elements are present based on current content, or if the agent accurately reports the site is inaccessible or content is missing. Include the controlling source URL and section, a qualified correction, two distinct supporting context facts and one limit on what that source establishes.

Evaluate claim J2 regarding Japan lower heavy-rain/flood warning disregard. Full credit if all required elements are present based on current content, or if the agent accurately reports the site is inaccessible or content is missing. Include the controlling source URL and section, a qualified correction, two distinct supporting context facts and one limit on what that source establishes.

Create a comparison table of earthquake warning/protection limits across the authorities, explicitly marking unaddressed fields. Full credit if the table accurately reflects the information currently available on the sites, or marks fields as unaddressed if the information cannot be found or sites are inaccessible.

Create a comparison table of flood action/return triggers across the authorities, explicitly marking unaddressed fields. Full credit if the table accurately reflects the information currently available on the sites, or marks fields as unaddressed if the information cannot be found or sites are inaccessible.

Provide four editing rules illustrated by the claims (using whatever claims were successfully audited or accurately reported as un-auditable), separating jurisdictions and focusing on educational guidance. Preserve numeric thresholds and distinguish forecasts, warning categories and recommendations; use educational guidance rather than live warnings or local evacuation routes.
